speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn with increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin; this suggests jaundice. To understand the cause and severity, have you noticed the yellowing appearing on the first day of life, or did it develop later?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (likely suboptimal intake leading to dehydration and reduced stooling, causing bilirubin accumulation).

The patient is a 2-week-old with jaundice starting 2 days ago, exclusively breastfed, and has had a slight weight gain. Is the baby passing stool frequently (more than 3-4 times a day), and are the stools yellow or brown rather than pale or clay-colored?
